lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach Marsilea as a rooted aquatic/amphibious heterosporous fern with four-part clover-like leaves and hard sporocarps, then separate the two project species primarily by sporocarp stalk and fruiting-body architecture rather than leaves.

project_scope.selection_mode: Marsilea macropoda + Marsilea vestita project module
project_scope.note: Both project species are accepted current concepts. Species-level field separation should prioritize fertile sporocarps because sterile water-clover leaves can be unreliable.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Trace a long petiole down to its base and look for a hard bean- or pea-like sporocarp. Above it, the blade is palmately divided into four clover-like pinnae.
family_diagnostics.vegetative: Aquatic or amphibious ferns with creeping rhizomes rooted in mud. Leaves arise on long petioles and in Marsilea terminate in four pinnae.
family_diagnostics.reproductive: Heterosporous. Hard sporocarps contain sori that produce both megaspores and microspores. When hydrated, the sporocarp opens and a gelatinous sorophore emerges carrying the sori.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Four-leaflet water-clover + hard sporocarp near the petiole base = Marsileaceae/Marsilea. If no sporocarps are present, stop short of a confident species call.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole rooted water-clover → sporocarp at petiole base → hydrated sporocarp opening → microspore vs megaspore → M. macropoda vs M. vestita sporocarp stalk → hybrid/intermediate caution
visual_lesson.intro: Marsilea looks like a four-leaf clover until you follow the petiole down. The hard little body near the base is the key: it is a fern sporocarp containing both male-sized microspores and female megaspores.

steps.title: 1 · Start with the four-part blade
steps.look_for: A long petiole ending in four leaflets/pinnae arranged like a clover.
steps.why_it_matters: This gives the family its fastest whole-plant gestalt, but it is only the starting point.

steps.title: 2 · Find the sporocarp at the petiole base
steps.look_for: A hard bean- or pea-like sporocarp attached near the base of the petiole on a short or elongated stalk.
steps.why_it_matters: The sporocarp confirms the plant is a heterosporous water-clover fern and carries the best species-level characters.

steps.title: 3 · Watch a sporocarp open after hydration
steps.look_for: The sporocarp splits and a gelatinous sorophore expands outward bearing multiple sori.
steps.why_it_matters: This converts an opaque hard 'seedlike' object into understandable fern reproductive anatomy.

steps.title: 4 · Separate microspores from megaspores
steps.look_for: Numerous tiny microspores versus much larger megaspores produced within the same sporocarp system.
steps.why_it_matters: Marsileaceae and Salviniaceae are unusual ferns because they are heterosporous rather than producing one spore type.

steps.title: 5 · Marsilea macropoda door
steps.look_for: Conspicuously hairy foliage; sporocarp stalks are commonly erect and can be branched, carrying strongly ascending hairy sporocarps.
steps.why_it_matters: Branched sporocarp stalks are one of the clearest project tie-breakers from M. vestita.

steps.title: 6 · Marsilea vestita door
steps.look_for: An unbranched sporocarp stalk from the petiole base; sporocarp usually perpendicular to slightly nodding, with a conspicuous distal tooth.
steps.why_it_matters: Fruit-body architecture is much safer than leaf shape for separating the two project species.

steps.title: 7 · Know the Blanco County hybrid problem
steps.look_for: Plants with mixed or intermediate M. macropoda/M. vestita characters.
steps.why_it_matters: FNA reports putative hybrids/intermediates in Blanco County, inside the project target zone, so ambiguous plants should not be forced to species.

comparisons.title: Marsileaceae vs Salviniaceae
comparisons.rule: Marsileaceae project plants are rooted in mud with long-petioled four-part leaves and hard sporocarps. Azolla in Salviniaceae is a tiny free-floating branched mat with overlapping scale leaves, hanging roots and tiny paired sporocarps.

comparisons.title: Marsilea vs true clover
comparisons.rule: Marsilea is a fern: no flowers, no fruits, and reproduction occurs through sporocarps and spores. Clover is a flowering legume with flowers and seeds.

comparisons.title: M. macropoda vs M. vestita
comparisons.rule: Use fertile characters as a suite: M. macropoda often has branched erect sporocarp stalks and very hairy foliage; M. vestita has unbranched stalks, more transverse/nodding sporocarps and a pronounced distal tooth. Hybrids/intermediates occur.

visual_lesson.caveat: Marsilea identification is often unreliable without sporocarps. Do not force a species ID from four-leaflet blades alone, especially in Central Texas where M. macropoda × M. vestita intermediates have been reported.

genera.fast_cue: rooted aquatic/amphibious fern + four-part clover-like blade + hard sporocarp near petiole base

taxonomy_reconciliation.note: Accepted by current Kew; native range includes central and southern Texas.
